findings.description: The wrapper now reuses one statistics dict per decorated function and clears it on every call, so overlapping calls share mutable state. A nested or recursive call, or a concurrent call from another thread, clears the dict that an in-flight outer call is still reading and writing.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a @retry-decorated function that calls itself recursively, or the same decorated function called from two threads at once. Mechanism: the inner or second call reaches stats.clear() on the shared dict, and copy._local.statistics aliases that same dict, so the outer call's attempt counts and timing are reset or overwritten. Impact: the outer call's wrapped_f.statistics reports wrong attempt_number and other values. The previous code gave each call a fresh dict, which the existing comment explicitly protected.
